speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
As yesterday, we will have the same languages.  If you need translation, English, French,  
Spanish and Hungarian. I will hand over to you.  Thanks. We will kick off with Tom Canton from  
Football London. That is okay. It is fine. Just  your initial thoughts? Pain. That is it. When  
you are so close in the competition and you are  a few penalty kicks away from winning the biggest  
football club competition, that is the way we  should feel. In 2006, it felt at that moment  
like it would be a long time that it would take  for us to get back there, but it does feel like  
this time you will be back in this position again  much sooner. Do you feel that as well? I do not  
know. We are going to have to earn that. The same  progression that we had in the last few years, we  
are going to have to do that over again. And the  level is increasing every single season. We had an  
incredible competition. We have not lost a single  match in the competition. But the reality is that  
when something had to go our way, especially in  the boxes, with the penalty that was given to  
Mosquera and then no penalty to Madueke, and the  penalty kicks, those margins did not go for us.  
James, CBS. Hi, Mikel. I know you said you are  feeling a lot of pain now, but is that mingled  
with pride? Because you came so close before that  penalty. It did not look like you would concede,  
for sure. What I said to the players and the  staff is that if I tell them one million times  
thank you, it is not going to be enough. And it  is not because we won the Premier League, and it  
is not because we played the cup final, it is not  because we played the Champions League final in  
the manner that we have done. It is because of the  joy and the moments that we have lived together  
every single day, and that is above anything  else. Alex from the BBC, to the left. Hi,  
Mikel. Hi. Can I ask about the penalty takers?  Gabriel, obviously, unfortunately, to miss the  
fifth penalty, but put in a great performance. I  know you had to take off a number of your regular  
takers as well, so how did he end up number five?  Did he put his hand up, or how had that come  
about? He wanted to take number five. Honestly, we  have prepared and trained this moment. Normally,  
the penalty takers would be Bukayo, would be  Martin, it would be Kai, for sure. And we knew  
that if we go to extra time and penalties, the  penalty takers will be different players. Still,  
with Gabi, when he practises penalties in  training, he does not miss any. But then  
you have to do it in this moment. We have been  unfortunate not to have the same precision and  
efficiency that they had, and that is the reason  that we have not won it. James, The Athletic. Hi,  
Mikel. Your team have shown in the Premier League  that they know how to respond to these kinds of  
disappointments, how to use this pain to motivate  them to come back, to push on. Is that what they  
need to replicate now in Europe, in the Champions  League? Yes. First of all, you have to go through  
that pain, digest it and turn it into fuel, as you  said, to improve and to reach a different level,  
because it will demand a different level with  the quality that is around Europe. I want to  
congratulate PSG, Luis in particular, because  they are, in my opinion, the best team in the  
world. What they are able to do with the ball,  with individual actions, I have not seen it. And  
it is not the plan to play in certain areas when  you do not have the ball, but they force you to do  
that. So even more credit to the players. Ed from  The Guardian. Hi, Mikel. You mentioned the penalty  
just earlier. Do you think that it was a  bit unfair on you, considering that they got  
given a penalty and you felt it was a penalty for  Arsenal? Well, it is comparing. I watched all the  
penalties in the competition in the last 72 hours  to understand what is a penalty and what is not,  
and that easily can be a penalty. Okay. Phil,  PA. Mikel, just following up on that, I suppose,  
over here on that penalty, I mean, that could have  won the match, obviously, for Arsenal and possibly  
the final. So it must be super frustrating.  If is not what happened, and that is it. So  
we need to do better. We will have to improve and  find different margins to get the outcome that we  
want. Okay. Sam from The Telegraph, on this  side. Hi, Mikel. You mentioned PSG being the  
best team in the world and the things they can do.  Is that what you look at now in terms of evolving  
your team and getting more towards that fluidity  and freedom? Perhaps, yes, and individual action  
that they have, for sure. And then you have to get  into the competition with all the squad available,  
in the best moment, each player. And we have  been with many more players than last season,  
but not all of them in that condition for  different reasons. And that is something that we  
have to improve as well. Okay, last two questions.  James, ESPN. Hi, Mikel. After such a long season,  
after the parade is out of the way, what do you do  the next few days? Do you switch off completely,  
or do you already start thinking about reviewing  and planning for next season? First of all, I will  
take a few days with my family and then we will  start the process to review what we have done,  
to start to make some very important decisions  if we want to reach another level. And we are  
going to have to show that ambition because we  are more than capable of doing it. But it is  
going to demand to be very, very ambitious, very  fast and very smart. And finally, Juan from Marca.  
So tomorrow you are going to have a million  people waiting for you in London. What are you  
going to say to these people? I would like to  thank all of these supporters on behalf of the  
team. They have carried us through the season. We  have had our lows, we have had difficult moments,  
and it has always been incredible and a  real pride for us to see them. When we won  
the Premier League after 22 years, obviously,  this is so painful. This is so painful for us,  
for them, that we have not come home with  the silverware. But I cannot even think  
about what it would have been like if we  had been taking it home. But tomorrow,  
it will still be a beautiful day. And for Madueke,  I think I have already answered this question.  
I have given my opinion already, so I  am not going to repeat it. Thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | PSG 1-1 Arsenal (Pens 4-3) | Champions League Final
